The prior finding required an observable release waiting/point-of-no-return seam for this interleaving.

current_disposition.reason: Closed: the candidate adds a per-lock-path release wait hook and the regression waits for that signal before resuming forget_group, eliminating the previously nondeterministic ordering.

evidence.locator: Lines 96-103: the condition only checks that release has not completed and that the lock still exists; it does not establish that release started or reached serialization.
Lines 8-13 require the regression to wait until release is observably past its point of no return, distinguishing a blocked fixed implementation from lock removal on the baseline.

origin.reason: The custody implementation serializes release and forget_group, and the standin waits for registration, but the new regression is not deterministic as specified. Immediately after Task.async, Task.yield(release_task, 0) can return nil before release has executed, while File.exists?(path) remains true; the test then resumes forget_group without proving release reached the critical section. On the unfixed implementation this can let forget_group write before release removes the lock, producing a false green test. Add an observable release-start/blocked seam or equivalent synchronization that proves the required interleaving before continuing forget_group.

intent.title: Fix the custody lock race and two flaky tests

evidence.locator: write_lock opens only an existing lock file; with_lock serializes lock-path operations and release removal.
record_group and forget_group perform their read-modify-write under with_lock; release wraps teardown and removal under the same lock.
Regression pauses forget_group after its read, observes release blocked on the same lock, resumes it, and verifies the lock is not recreated.
Stop-mode stand-in waits until read_lock reports a registered group before READY and release.

scenarios.reason: Satisfied: production lock updates and release/removal are serialized per expanded lock path, writes cannot recreate a removed file, and the regression deterministically proves the required interleaving and post-release absence. The stop stand-in uses registration polling instead of a fixed sleep.

evidence.locator: Readiness assertions retain the probe message while checking status 0 for success and status 1 for failure; no timeout values or test names changed.
The installer failure matrix builds incomplete_payload once and reuses the same bytes for registry and fetch, while preserving integrity and credential assertions.

scenarios.reason: Satisfied: probe status assertions now report the diagnostic message, and the omitted-package installer case reuses one archive payload without weakening assertions, renaming tests, or changing deadlines.
